posts.title: A Concurrency Group Is a Discard Policy
posts.summary: A concurrency group is not merely a resource limit. It defines whether later work replaces earlier work, whether an in-progress operation can be interrupted, and which commit never receives a result.

posts.title: An Environment Variable Is a Deployment-Time API
posts.summary: Parse configuration once at startup, validate it into a named schema, and surface the effective non-secret settings. Deployment configuration deserves an API contract.

posts.title: An Empty Search Result Is Not Evidence That Nothing Exists
posts.summary: `[]` can mean no matches, an incomplete index, a permission boundary, a truncated search, or a query against yesterday's snapshot. Make a tool state which of those it means before an agent tells a user that no record exists.

posts.title: A Date Is Not a Timestamp
posts.summary: Keep civil dates, local date-times, and instants as different types. A bare YYYY-MM-DD should not pass through a timestamp parser merely because both happen to use ISO-looking text.

posts.title: Starting a Job Is Not the Same as Finishing It
posts.summary: A successful call can mean that work was accepted, not that its external effect happened. Model long-running work as an operation with a durable status and make agents distinguish started from completed.

posts.title: A Tool Error Is an Instruction to Your Agent
posts.summary: Tool errors are part of an agent's control loop. Return a bounded, typed recovery signal so the agent can distinguish a repairable request from a policy denial, a rate limit, and an action whose completion is unknown.

posts.title: A Valid JSON Response Can Still Be a Bad Answer
posts.summary: A response schema proves the shape of an answer, not whether an answer should be given. Include explicit states for missing evidence, ambiguity, and refusal so a valid object can also be an honest one.

posts.title: Prompt Caching Makes Prompt Layout a Production Interface
posts.summary: A prompt cache reuses an exact rendered prefix, not an abstract idea of a similar prompt. Structure stable context deliberately, put volatile work at the tail, and measure cache changes like any other production interface change.

posts.title: Agent Tool Calls Need Traces, Not Just Logs
posts.summary: Tool logs answer what ran. A trace answers which agent decision caused it, what it waited on, and whether the failure belongs to the model, orchestration, or downstream service.

posts.title: Repository Context Is a Dependency, Not a Prompt Attachment
posts.summary: Give coding agents a deliberate repository slice: the relevant code, tests, policy files, and current Git state. More files are not automatically more context.
